newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end lower in thin trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended lower in thin trading that saw some market movers fall on profit-taking and disappointing third quarter earnings.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index fell 0.22 percent to end at 13,493.16 on a lower-than-average volume of 495 million pesos while Bogota's IBB slipped 0.26 percent to 872.36 on lackluster volume of 866 million pesos.

Brokers said trading was thinner than usual because many market players had taken the day off, or left early, in advance of the three-day holiday weekend. Financial markets will be closed Monday in observance of the All Saints holiday.

Losers in Bogota were led by Cadenalco, the country's largest retailer in terms of both size and sales, which dropped 2.17 percent to 900 pesos a share. Its rival Carulla also ended sharply lower, dropping 1.69 percent to close at 5,800 pesos per share.
Both companies reported what brokers described as lower-than-expected earnings earlier this week. Cadenalco reported a 32 percent fall in net income during the first nine months of the year.
Banco de Bogota, whose nine-month earnings nearly doubled over last year, was also hit by profit-taking, however.
The bank, which is Colombia's oldest and has its largest retail branch network, ended down 0.97 percent at 6,090 pesos per share.
Brewer Bavaria S.A. also ended lower, falling 0.63 percent to close at 4,063 pesos a share, as did blue-chip Banco Ganadero, which dropped 0.36 percent to end at 271 pesos a share.

Losers in Medellin included cement maker Cementos Argos, which fell 0.93 percent to end at 5,350 pesos a share and cigarette maker Coltabaco, which dropped 0.33 percent to end the day at 3,000 pesos per share.
